findings.scenario: A consumer installs prismarine-world in production without development dependencies or its own prismarine-block installation.
findings.evidence: world.js now unconditionally requires prismarine-block, while the supplied package.json lists only vec3 as a runtime dependency. Loading World can therefore fail with MODULE_NOT_FOUND; development dependency hoisting can conceal this.

findings.scenario: Storage saving rejects before the shutdown timeout expires.
findings.evidence: The await in saveAndQuit rejects before reaching clearTimeout(timer), leaving the timeout active for the remainder of the default ten seconds even though shutdown has already failed.
findings.requested_change: Clear the timeout in a finally block so both successful and rejected saves release it.
findings.validation: Stub waitSaving to reject immediately and verify the rejection is preserved and no timeout remains scheduled.

findings.scenario: A caller substitutes getCachedBlock for getBlock and reads position-dependent properties or mutates the returned object.
findings.evidence: The cache stores one fromStateId object per state and returns it for all positions; unlike getBlock it never fills position from the query and never reads per-position block fields. Documentation describes a block at the given position without explaining this shared state-only contract.
findings.requested_change: Document that cached values are shared templates and which position-dependent fields are unavailable, and warn callers against mutating them.
findings.validation: Document and demonstrate that two positions with the same state return the same object and cannot independently retain position-specific fields.

findings.scenario: A consumer installs prismarine-world alone with production dependencies and requires it, even without using block caching.
findings.evidence: The new top-level require loads prismarine-block unconditionally, but the supplied package.json dependencies contains only vec3. Development transitive dependencies can mask this missing runtime dependency.
findings.requested_change: Declare a compatible prismarine-block version in runtime dependencies.
findings.validation: Smoke-test requiring the packed package in a clean production-only installation. Static manifest/import trace; not executed.
findings.skills_help: Architecture and protocol integration guidance required checking what consumers actually install rather than relying on a development tree.

findings.scenario: The storage provider rejects a save before saveAndQuit reaches its timeout.
findings.evidence: waitSaving propagates saveNow rejection through Promise.race, so the await throws and skips clearTimeout(timer). The newly created timeout remains active, delaying process shutdown for the remaining timeout despite saveAndQuit promising to stop timers.
findings.requested_change: Clear the timeout in a finally block so both successful saves and save failures release it.
findings.validation: Use a rejecting storage provider and a long timeout; verify the original rejection reaches the caller and no timeout remains active. Static completion-path trace; not executed.
findings.skills_help: Code-quality guidance focused on error ownership and cleanup on every completion path, without mistaking the propagated rejection for a swallowed error.

findings.scenario: A caller uses the documented getCachedBlock(pos) result as the block at that position, including its position or per-location light/biome state.
findings.evidence: buildBlockCache creates one Block.fromStateId object per state, and getCachedBlock returns it without reading positional fields from the chunk or assigning position. The existing getBlock explicitly obtains chunk block data and sets position. Two coordinates with the same state therefore return the same context-free mutable object, so the new API does not provide the documented block at the requested position.
findings.requested_change: Define and preserve the returned object contract: either return a position-correct block with its per-location data, or expose this explicitly as a shared read-only state template and document its omitted fields and aliasing instead of promising a normal positional block.
findings.validation: Compare cached and ordinary reads at two coordinates sharing a state but having different light/biome values; verify the documented position and mutation semantics. Static trace; not executed.
findings.skills_help: Architecture guidance separated shared semantic state from contextual objects; behavior-test guidance showed that the single stateId assertion does not cover the documented result contract.

findings.scenario: On the newPlayerInputPacket path, the caller has already enabled sneak before invoking dismount, for example issuing both operations before the next physics tick.
findings.evidence: The new finally block always calls setControlState(sneak, false), regardless of the pre-existing control state. A dismount therefore clears a caller-held sneak control after leaving the vehicle, whereas the prior dismount only wrote its packet.
findings.requested_change: Capture the previous sneak state before the temporary pulse and restore it in finally. Cover initially true and initially false states.
findings.validation: Start with sneak true, invoke dismount, advance its tick, and assert the prior state is preserved; repeat with sneak false and a rejected tick wait. Static state trace; not executed.
findings.skills_help: Architecture guidance tracked ownership of the caller control state, and code-quality guidance checked what cleanup restores rather than only whether a finally block exists.

findings.scenario: The change relies on one real physics tick carrying sneak into a player_input packet, but the new regression test replaces both control-setting and tick-waiting with spies.
findings.evidence: The asserted event array proves the chosen calls occur in order; it does not exercise input packet generation or establish that a server actually removes the vehicle attachment. The crucial control-to-packet boundary is bypassed.
findings.requested_change: Add focused coverage using the actual control/tick pipeline and inspect the resulting player_input shift field, or reuse a server mount/dismount test that observes the authoritative detach on a modern version.
findings.validation: The regression should fail with the previous jump-only request and pass only when the real outgoing input or server detach confirms the new behavior.
findings.skills_help: Behavior-test guidance distinguished implementation-spy assertions from packet delivery and server-observed action, keeping the broader validation request optional.
